title: Most Roman theologians agree with the Reformed that Adam was created in that righteousness
source_text: XLII. Inde quoque manifestum est, Scholae Romanae Theologos, plerosque saltem, cum Reformatis docere primum hominem fuisse in justitia illa & sanctitate creatum; adeoque primum hominem nunquam ea caruisse, sed eam illi a prima Origine fuisse insitam.
pass_a_gloss: Thence also it is manifest that the Theologians of the Roman School, at least most of them, teach with the Reformed that the first man was created in that justice and sanctity; and so that the first man never lacked it, but that it was implanted in him from the first Origin.
pass_b_english: It is also clear from this that most theologians of the Roman school, at least, teach with the Reformed that the first man was created in that righteousness and holiness. He was therefore never without it; it was planted in him from his first origin.

choices.why: Origo is the moment of creation; 'origin' keeps the link with 'original righteousness'.
rejected: from the beginning of the world
